idiom_name: Express/connect middleware functions (req, res, next) with app.use ordering
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the interception layer is the middleware chain: each function receives (req, res, next), validates the request and either responds with a rejection (never calling next()) or calls next() to continue, and app.use registration order is the chain order - the Express guide's own example is a cookie-validating middleware. Schema checks are ordinary functions or a schema library, so the plain-function idiom replaces the classic interceptor object graph with no framework import beyond the one already in use. Mount the validator on the router (router.use) rather than per route so every route of that router is covered by construction.
pitfalls: Middleware registered after the route it should protect never runs, and a terminating route ends the cycle; mount validation on the router before its routes.

Calling next() before async validation settles lets the handler run on unvalidated data (Express 5 forwards rejected promises, but an explicit early return after res.status(...) is still required to avoid a double send).
Middleware that mutates req.body in place hides the canonical form; keep the raw payload and publish the validated value on a dedicated property.
